note: task texts: scenario name, blurb, actions, rules and the linked station's step titles, prompts and hazards (exports/unity stations); stations also have one text per drill step (stepInstructions, keyed by the line's step)

instructions.rb-cell-entry: Robot Cell Entry. Walk up to a working robot cell, watch it slow and stop as you near, test the e-stop, lock out, check for zero energy, clear the jam and restart safely.. walk {d} (m, + toward the cell) test-estop press-estop lockout verify enter clear-jam exit remove-lock restart wait. rule enter-live-cell rule skip-estop-test rule lockout-order rule no-verify rule restart-with-lock rule left-locked. SmartCiti.X~ Robot Cell Lockout & Safe Re-entry VR A fenced robot cell entered the only way that keeps a person out of the arm's reach: stopped, isolated at the disconnect with your own lock, stored energy proven gone, the pendant in reduced speed if anything must move, and the cell restored only after a head count and a clear floor Suit up for the cell. Safety glasses, safety shoes and cut-resistant gloves before the gate. Read the lockout procedure. Confirm every energy source the cell's written procedure lists before touching anything. Bring the cell to a normal stop. Use the cycle stop to end the program at a safe point. Isolate and lock out. Open the disconnect, hang your own lock and tag, then dump the air. Try the start. Press the cell start to prove it will not run. Verify zero energy. Read the cell's energy check and commit only once it reads zero. Block the raised axis. Carry the block to the arm's rest point and seat it under the raised axis. Jog in reduced speed. With the pendant in reduced speed, keep the jog inside the band while the arm moves clear. Find the cause. Look along the shelf for what caused the jam. Bleed the trapped air. Hold the bleed valve open until the line gauge falls to nothing. Remove the block. Take the axis block out once the work under the arm is done. Clear the cell. Count everyone out and check the floor for tools before the lock comes off. Check the guarding. Before restart, find the guard that is not doing its job. Remove your lock and log it. Remove your own lock, restore energy per the procedure and log the entry. That hangs a coworker's lock on the disconnect for you. A lock only protects the person who holds its key; if somebody else can take it off, it is protecting them, not you. That jumpers the gate interlock so the cell keeps running with the gate open. An interlock defeated for convenience is a guard that is not there, and it is the one piece of the cell designed for the day somebody forgets. That walks under the raised arm without blocking it. An axis held up by its brake can drop when the brake is released or fails, and the arm does not need power to move downward. That reaches over the light curtain to clear the part with the arm in automatic. A curtain stops the arm when it sees a body break the beam; a hand reaching over the top may never break it at all.
instructions.rb-cobot-zone-setup: Cobot Safety-Zone Setup. Set a cobot's warning and stop zones for its speed, test the area scanner and the e-stop, then commit the setup.. set {param: warn|stop|speed, value} test {what: scanner|estop|zone-walk} commit wait. rule zone-too-small rule warn-inside-stop rule skip-scanner-test rule skip-estop-test. SmartCiti.X~ Cobot Risk Assessment & Speed-and-Separation VR A collaborative robot bench brought into service the way a risk assessment demands: the application walked task by task, the area scanner's warning and protective zones proven with a body, speed-and-separation shown to slow and stop the arm, and the bench released only when every hazard on the sheet has a control that was actually tested Prepare for the bench. Safety glasses, safety shoes and long hair tied back before the bench. Open the risk assessment. Open the application's risk assessment and read the hazards it lists. Walk the application. Walk the operator's tasks, then check the gripper and the layout against the sheet. Check the area scanner. Check the area scanner's window is clean and unobstructed. Prove the zones with a body. Walk into the warning zone and watch the arm slow, then into the protective zone and watch it stop. Check the stopping performance. Read the stopping check and commit only in the green band the manual sets. Stage the part. Carry a part blank to the fixture tray. Walk the approach. Keep your approach to the bench steady inside the band as the arm runs. Find the unassessed hazard. Look along the shelf for the hazard the sheet does not cover. Run the contact check. Hold the contact check through the test the manual describes. Release the bench. With every control tested, release the bench for use. Update the risk assessment. Add the sharp corner and its guard to the sheet. Check the pendant. Before you leave, find the setting that should not be left as it is. Sign the release. Sign the release log with the tests run and the sheet updated. That mutes the area scanner so the arm stops slowing when you lean in. Speed-and-separation is the control; muting it turns a collaborative application into an unguarded robot with a person beside it. That signs the scanner zones off from the settings screen without walking into them. Settings say what the scanner should do; only a body walking into the zone shows what it actually does. That raises the arm's speed to hit the cycle time without reassessing. Speed changes the separation the arm needs, and a new speed means a new assessment, not a quicker version of the old one. That fits the sharp-edged finger set the assessment never covered. The collaborative assessment was done for the gripper on the sheet; a new tool with edges is a new hazard the sheet does not answer.
instructions.rb-teleop-pick-place: Teleop Pick-and-Place. Guide a robot gripper to move parts from the bin to the fixture, gripping each part within its force limit and keeping clear of your teammate's space.. move {dx,dy,dz} (m, capped at params.speed per step) grip {force} (N) release estop reset wait. rule over-force rule keep-out. instructions.rb-amr-fleet-routing: AMR Fleet Routing. Route a small fleet of warehouse robots to their drop-offs without two robots claiming the same spot, and hold them at the walkway while a person crosses.. route {moves: [N|S|E|W|wait per robot]} estop wait. rule conflict rule yield-missed. SmartCiti.X~ AMR Fleet Traffic & E-stop Drill VR A floor shared with autonomous mobile robots worked the way the traffic plan intends: people on the walkways and robots on the marked lanes, crossings made only at the marked points, an e-stop drill that proves every robot actually stops, and a fault robot recovered only after it is taken out of the fleet Dress for the floor. Hi-vis vest, safety shoes and safety glasses before you step onto the floor. Read the traffic plan. Find today's lanes, crossings and closed zones before walking onto the floor. Cross at the marked point. Walk to the marked crossing, look both ways and cross. Run the e-stop drill. Trigger the drill and confirm each robot on the lane has actually stopped. Check the unit's scanner field. Read the scanner field check and commit only in the green band. Take the faulted unit out of the fleet. At the fleet console, take unit 14 out of the fleet before touching it. Close the lane. Carry the lane barrier to the lane mouth and set it. Push the unit to the bay. In manual mode, keep the push steady inside the band as the unit rolls to the service bay. Find the cause. Look along the shelf for what took the unit off its lane. Hold the lane closed. Hold the lane closure on the console while the unit is inspected. Return the unit to the fleet. Return unit 14 to the fleet once the cause is cleared and the scanner checks green. Reopen the lane. Remove the barrier and reopen the lane on the console. Walk the lane. Before you leave, find what makes this lane less safe than the plan says. Log the drill and the recovery. Log the e-stop results, the fault cause and the missing mirror. That hangs a jacket over the robot's scanner to stop it slowing near the bench. A robot that cannot see is a robot that will not stop for the next person, and its safety comes entirely from that scanner. That cuts across the live lane between two robots. A robot's scanner is set to slow and stop for what it can see, but a person stepping out from behind a rack or another robot may be inside its stopping distance before it sees them. That pushes the faulted robot by hand while it is still in the fleet. A unit the controller still thinks is available can be given a new mission and start moving under your hands. That stands on the robot's lift plate to reach the shelf. The lift plate carries loads, not people, and the robot has no way to know a person is riding it when it decides to move.
instructions.rb-construction-drilling: Ceiling-Drilling Robot Set-Up. Set a ceiling-drilling robot to work on a concrete deck: scan the deck, set the barricade, switch the dust collection on, drill the layout and change a worn bit with the battery isolated. Hold the robot whenever a person steps inside the barricade.. scan barricade dust-on drill hold isolate change-bit restore estop wait. rule person-in-barricade rule drill-unscanned rule no-barricade rule dust-off rule bit-change-live. SmartCiti.X~ Ceiling-Drilling Robot Set-Up VR Setting up a mobile ceiling-drilling robot on a concrete deck: the scan for embedded conduit and tendons read before any hole, the work zone barricaded so nobody stands under the mast, the robot's position checked against control points, the drill's vacuum dust collection running, a bit changed only with the battery isolated, and the dust cleaned with a vacuum instead of a broom Read the work plan for the deck. Read the work plan: the bay, the anchor layout, the robot's zone and who runs it. Read the deck scan. Read the scan of the slab for embedded conduit, tendons and rebar against the layout. Dress for overhead drilling. Hard hat, safety glasses and hearing protection. Barricade the robot's reach. Carry the barricade stand to the corner mark so the tape encloses the robot's full reach. Check the robot's position on the control points. Check the robot's position against the control points and commit only when the readout is in the green. Connect the dust collection. Connect the drill's shroud to the vacuum dust collector and confirm it is running. Find the hole you must not drill. Find the layout hole that lands on an embedded service in the scan. Hold enable while it drives to hole one. Hold the controller's enable while the robot drives to the first position. Watch the vacuum flow through the first holes. Keep the dust collector's flow inside the band while the first holes are drilled. Change the bit the safe way. Stop the drill and lower the mast, isolate and lock the battery, then change the bit. Clean up with the HEPA vacuum. Clean the dust on the deck and the robot with the HEPA-filtered vacuum. Log the as-drilled holes. Log the holes drilled, the one removed for the conduit, and the bit changes for the foreperson. That sweeps the drilling dust into a pile with a broom. Concrete dust carries respirable crystalline silica, and dry sweeping lifts the finest part of it into the air the crew breathes; the cleanup is done with a vacuum fitted with a HEPA filter. That changes the drill bit with the battery still connected and the robot only paused. A paused robot can resume on a command from the tablet, and the hands on the bit are the closest thing to the motor when it does. That starts drilling straight from the layout without reading the deck scan. A layout shows where the anchors should go, not what is already inside the slab, and a bit that finds a live conduit or a stressed tendon finds it the hard way. That walks under the raised mast to pick up a dropped anchor while the robot is drilling. The drill head, the bit and the concrete chips all come down from above, and the barricade exists so that nobody's head is ever where the robot is working.

rb-station-robot-cell.ppe: Suit up for the cell. Safety glasses, safety shoes and cut-resistant gloves before the gate.. The inside of a robot cell is full of fixtures, sheet edges and parts at hand height, and the gloves and glasses are there for the ordinary cuts and flying clips of clearing a jam, not for the arm, which only isolation protects you from.
rb-station-robot-cell.brief: Read the lockout procedure. Confirm every energy source the cell's written procedure lists before touching anything.. A robot cell usually carries more than one energy source — electrical, pneumatic, sometimes a gravity-loaded axis — and the written procedure is what lists them all, so none is missed because it was not the one you were thinking about.
rb-station-robot-cell.stop-cell: Bring the cell to a normal stop. Use the cycle stop to end the program at a safe point.. A normal cycle stop parks the arm at the end of its motion instead of freezing it mid-path with a part in the gripper, which is what makes the isolation that follows a controlled one rather than a scramble.
rb-station-robot-cell.isolate: Isolate and lock out. Open the disconnect, hang your own lock and tag, then dump the air.. Opening the disconnect removes the power, your own lock makes sure only you can restore it, and dumping the air removes the second source that could still close a gripper or push a slide — in that order, so no step relies on one that has not happened yet.
rb-station-robot-cell.try-start: Try the start. Press the cell start to prove it will not run.. The try-start is the test that turns 'I opened the disconnect' into 'this cell cannot move' — a wrong breaker, a second feed or a bypassed circuit shows up here, harmlessly, instead of when someone is inside.
rb-station-robot-cell.zero-energy: Verify zero energy. Read the cell's energy check and commit only once it reads zero.. Stored energy outlives the switch — a capacitor bank, trapped air in a line, a spring-loaded clamp — and the meter reading is what shows that the energy the procedure listed is actually gone rather than merely disconnected.
rb-station-robot-cell.block-axis: Block the raised axis. Carry the block to the arm's rest point and seat it under the raised axis.. An axis held up only by its brake can drop without any power at all, and a mechanical block under it is what makes working beneath the arm safe even if that brake is released or fails.
rb-station-robot-cell.jog-reduced: Jog in reduced speed. With the pendant in reduced speed, keep the jog inside the band while the arm moves clear.. Teaching or jogging inside the cell is done in the reduced-speed mode the manufacturer's manual sets, with the enabling switch held, so that a person close to the arm always has time to react and a single release stops it.
rb-station-robot-cell.find-damage: Find the cause. Look along the shelf for what caused the jam.. Clearing a jam without finding its cause means the cell will jam again, probably on the next shift, and the frayed cable found now is also a live electrical hazard the moment power comes back.
rb-station-robot-cell.bleed-air: Bleed the trapped air. Hold the bleed valve open until the line gauge falls to nothing.. The dump valve empties the supply, but air trapped between a closed valve and a cylinder can still move a clamp when a fitting is loosened, and holding the bleed open is how that last pocket is let out on purpose.
rb-station-robot-cell.remove-block: Remove the block. Take the axis block out once the work under the arm is done.. The block comes out before restart because an arm driven into its own block can damage itself or throw the block, and every tool and block brought into the cell has to come back out with the person who brought it.
rb-station-robot-cell.clear-cell: Clear the cell. Count everyone out and check the floor for tools before the lock comes off.. Restoring energy is only safe once every person is outside the fence and nothing is left inside for the arm to hit, and the head count is the one check that makes the first of those a fact.
rb-station-robot-cell.find-open-gate: Check the guarding. Before restart, find the guard that is not doing its job.. Guards and interlocks are checked before restart, not assumed, because a gate that looks shut but has not made its interlock is a gate that will not stop the arm the next time somebody opens it.
rb-station-robot-cell.closeout: Remove your lock and log it. Remove your own lock, restore energy per the procedure and log the entry.. The lock comes off only by the hand that put it on, after the head count and the guard check, and the log is what tells the next shift what was done inside their cell and what still needs parts.

rb-station-amr-fleet.ppe: Dress for the floor. Hi-vis vest, safety shoes and safety glasses before you step onto the floor.. A robot floor is shared with lift trucks and tuggers driven by people, and the hi-vis vest is for their eyes, not the robots' — the robots' scanners see a body either way, but a driver turning a corner needs every bit of contrast they can get.
rb-station-amr-fleet.brief: Read the traffic plan. Find today's lanes, crossings and closed zones before walking onto the floor.. Robot lanes and crossings change when the floor layout changes, and the traffic plan is what shows today's version — walking the floor from memory means walking yesterday's lanes.
rb-station-amr-fleet.cross-lane: Cross at the marked point. Walk to the marked crossing, look both ways and cross.. The marked crossing is where robots are configured to slow and where they expect people, and it is the only place where the floor's design has already done half the work of keeping you out of a robot's path.
rb-station-amr-fleet.estop-drill: Run the e-stop drill. Trigger the drill and confirm each robot on the lane has actually stopped.. An e-stop drill proves the stop works on every unit, not just the one the technician happened to check last month, and a robot that keeps rolling on the drill is found now instead of on the day somebody needs it to stop.
rb-station-amr-fleet.scanner-check: Check the unit's scanner field. Read the scanner field check and commit only in the green band.. The robot's scanner is the thing that slows and stops it for people, and the field check is what shows it is clean, aligned and seeing the zone the risk assessment says it should, not a smudged window guessing.
rb-station-amr-fleet.recover-select: Take the faulted unit out of the fleet. At the fleet console, take unit 14 out of the fleet before touching it.. A faulted robot the controller still counts as available can be handed a new mission at any moment, and taking it out of the fleet at the console is what guarantees it will not start moving while a person is next to it.
rb-station-amr-fleet.close-lane: Close the lane. Carry the lane barrier to the lane mouth and set it.. The barrier tells the fleet and every driver on the floor that this lane is closed, so the recovery happens inside a space nothing else is routed through rather than in a gap between moving robots.
rb-station-amr-fleet.escort-push: Push the unit to the bay. In manual mode, keep the push steady inside the band as the unit rolls to the service bay.. A robot pushed in manual mode has no drive holding it back, and a steady push inside the band keeps it under your control instead of rolling on its own into a rack or a person's ankles.
rb-station-amr-fleet.find-cause: Find the cause. Look along the shelf for what took the unit off its lane.. A robot that faulted once will fault again unless the cause is found, and the floor debris wound into a caster is also a sign the lane itself needs sweeping before the next unit runs over it.
rb-station-amr-fleet.hold-lane-closed: Hold the lane closed. Hold the lane closure on the console while the unit is inspected.. The lane stays closed on the console for the whole inspection, not only until the barrier is in place, because a fleet that reopens the lane on its own schedule can route a unit into the space you are working in.
rb-station-amr-fleet.return-unit: Return the unit to the fleet. Return unit 14 to the fleet once the cause is cleared and the scanner checks green.. A unit rejoins the fleet only after its fault is cleared and its scanner is proven, because putting it back early turns a known fault into an unexpected one somewhere else on the floor.
rb-station-amr-fleet.reopen: Reopen the lane. Remove the barrier and reopen the lane on the console.. Reopening is done deliberately at both the barrier and the console so that the floor and the fleet agree the lane is live again, instead of one thinking it is closed while the other sends robots through it.
rb-station-amr-fleet.find-blind-corner: Walk the lane. Before you leave, find what makes this lane less safe than the plan says.. The traffic plan assumes the floor matches it, and a missing mirror at a blind corner is the kind of gap that lets a person and a robot meet with no warning, so it is reported now rather than noticed after a near miss.
rb-station-amr-fleet.closeout: Log the drill and the recovery. Log the e-stop results, the fault cause and the missing mirror.. The fleet log is how a pattern shows up — the same unit faulting, the same corner causing trouble — and a drill and a recovery that are not written down teach the floor nothing.

rb-station-cobot.ppe: Prepare for the bench. Safety glasses, safety shoes and long hair tied back before the bench.. Working beside a moving arm means loose hair, sleeves and lanyards are the things that get caught first, and the glasses protect against a part flicked from the gripper, which the arm's own safety functions do nothing about.
rb-station-cobot.brief: Open the risk assessment. Open the application's risk assessment and read the hazards it lists.. A collaborative application is only collaborative because a risk assessment showed its hazards are controlled for this task, this tool and this layout, and the sheet is where those findings live and where any change has to be written first.
rb-station-cobot.walk-tasks: Walk the application. Walk the operator's tasks, then check the gripper and the layout against the sheet.. The assessment is only valid for the tasks, tool and layout it describes, and walking each against the bench as it stands today is how a changed fixture or a swapped gripper is caught before it becomes the hazard nobody assessed.
rb-station-cobot.clean-scanner: Check the area scanner. Check the area scanner's window is clean and unobstructed.. The area scanner is what the arm relies on to know where people are, and a smudged or obstructed window can make it see a person too late or not at all, which undoes speed-and-separation without any warning on the screen.
rb-station-cobot.zone-test: Prove the zones with a body. Walk into the warning zone and watch the arm slow, then into the protective zone and watch it stop.. Speed-and-separation only works if the arm really slows and stops at the zones the assessment set, and the only honest test is a person walking into them while the arm runs, because a settings screen shows intent, not behaviour.
rb-station-cobot.stop-time: Check the stopping performance. Read the stopping check and commit only in the green band the manual sets.. The separation distance depends on how quickly the arm actually stops, and a stopping check outside its band means the zones drawn on the floor are too small for the arm as it behaves today.
rb-station-cobot.stage-part: Stage the part. Carry a part blank to the fixture tray.. Parts are staged in the tray the assessment describes so that the operator's hands go only where the analysis expected them, rather than into the arm's path to rescue a part set down somewhere convenient.
rb-station-cobot.approach-walk: Walk the approach. Keep your approach to the bench steady inside the band as the arm runs.. The zones are calibrated for a person walking at a normal pace, and a steady approach inside the band shows the arm slowing smoothly rather than stopping abruptly, which tells you the separation is set right for real use.
rb-station-cobot.find-gap: Find the unassessed hazard. Look along the shelf for the hazard the sheet does not cover.. Walking the bench always turns up something the desk review missed, and a sharp corner where the arm can trap a hand is exactly the kind of detail that decides whether contact is harmless or not.
rb-station-cobot.force-hold: Run the contact check. Hold the contact check through the test the manual describes.. Where the application relies on limiting contact force, the check is run through its whole cycle with the manufacturer's test method, because a partial check proves nothing about the moment the arm actually meets a hand.
rb-station-cobot.release-select: Release the bench. With every control tested, release the bench for use.. Release is the statement that every hazard on the sheet has a control and every control has been tested, and releasing on anything less is releasing on hope rather than on the evidence the assessment asked for.
rb-station-cobot.update-sheet: Update the risk assessment. Add the sharp corner and its guard to the sheet.. A hazard found and fixed but not written into the assessment will be missed again the next time the bench is changed, and updating the sheet is how the finding outlives the person who found it.
rb-station-cobot.find-pendant: Check the pendant. Before you leave, find the setting that should not be left as it is.. A pendant left in the wrong mode is how the next person teaching the arm finds it moving faster than they expect, so it is returned to the state the procedure sets before the bench is left.
rb-station-cobot.closeout: Sign the release. Sign the release log with the tests run and the sheet updated.. The release log records who tested what and when, so that when the bench changes, the next person knows what the last release was based on and what needs testing again.
